originality.rationale: Maass–Turán (1992, printed p.139) supplies precisely the full-symmetric-group forest shattering criterion, but its every-orientation extension argument does not cover parity-restricted existence; the new theorem pinpoints the unique-extension Hamiltonian path exceptions and counts even-permutation shattered maximum supports. Walker (2022) proves general tree-shattering theory, Raz (2000) defines a different permutation VC invariant, and Berendsohn–Kozma–Marx (2019) treats pattern constraints. Exact published-finding corpus searches and checked accessible prior claims did not identify the stated parity criterion, modulo-four maximum-support count, or precise seven-label Littlestone value; this supports a provisional originality judgment, not a proof of absolute priority.

value.rationale: A natural index-two restriction of the total-order concept class preserves VC dimension at n>=4 but creates an exact parity-sensitive set of excluded maximal shattered supports, with an all-order modulo-four count. The same class has a sharp finite adaptive threshold at seven labels, where the cardinality bound first fails. This provides a structural obstruction and a reproducible exact cutoff, not merely a relabeling of unrestricted linear orders.
